samples.question: This page shows one black line figure together with several coloured decorations. Only the black figure and the two solid dots matter; blue, orange, grey and purple marks are decoration and never count, even when a decoration is drawn as a closed ring with its own hole. The black figure is a single trace: every black stroke on the page is joined to the rest of the black ink, and the trace runs in straight horizontal and vertical stretches that meet at square corners. Somewhere along the trace the strokes close up into a complete circuit, and somewhere else they almost close into a second circuit that is interrupted by one visible gap. Exactly one solid green dot and exactly one solid red dot are drawn on the page, far apart from each other, and neither dot touches any black stroke. A dot counts as shut in only when you cannot travel from that dot to the edge of the page without crossing a black stroke; a gap in the strokes is a way through, however far from the dot it lies. Exactly one of the two dots is shut in and the other is not. How large the black figure is, how much black ink it holds, where on the page each dot sits, which dot looks more surrounded, and how many coloured decorations are drawn never decide the answer. Which dot is shut in, the green dot or the red dot? Answer green or red.
